title: Solvent Extraction of PDMS Tubing for Volatile Organic Compounds Capture
author: Gareth Thomas

steps.title: Prepare PDMS Tubing
steps.instruction: Cut PDMS tubing (1 mm i.d. × 0.4 mm wall thickness) to the required length.

substeps.instruction: For headspace VOC collections: 2.5 cm - 7.5 cm
For synthetic VOC blend collection from rhizosphere: 30 cm
For root VOC collection from rhizosphere: 130 cm

steps.title: Condition PDMS Tubing
steps.instruction: Clean and heat-treat the PDMS tubing to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Soak cut pieces of PDMS tubing in 100% methanol for a minimum of 24 hours.
Place tubing into a glass vessel.
Attach the glass vessel to a constant flow of purified nitrogen, ensuring tubing faces the direction of the flow.
Place the vessel in a modified heating oven at 170°C for a minimum of 1.5 hours.
Remove the vessel using heat-resistant gloves and allow to cool while maintaining nitrogen flow.

steps.title: Prepare Glassware and Plates
steps.instruction: Clean and sterilize the collection chamber and metal plates.

substeps.instruction: Wash the glass chamber (6 cm height × 12 cm diam.) and 250 mL glass beakers with Teepol detergent and rinse with distilled water.
Rinse the glass chamber and beakers with 100% acetone.
Place the glass chamber and metal plates (12 cm diam.) in a modified heating oven at 150°C for a minimum of 1.5 hours (beakers for a minimum of 2 hours).
Remove using heat-resistant gloves and allow to cool.

steps.title: Set Up Headspace Collection (Synthetic VOCs)
steps.instruction: Assemble the chamber for synthetic VOC blend capture.

substeps.instruction: Place a filter paper disc (12.5 cm) onto a metal plate (12 cm diam.).
Place a Petri dish (5 cm diam.) on top of the filter paper.
Place a small filter paper disc (0.6 cm diam.) onto the Petri dish.
Cover the glass chamber outlet with a small square of tin foil.
Use forceps to insert a small hole through the tin foil.
Using cotton gloves, insert the conditioned PDMS tubing through the hole so it is suspended above the headspace.
Attach the septum and red screw cap to the inlet at the side of the glass chamber.
Apply 10 µL of a synthetic VOC blend (10 µg/µL blend for a 100 µg dose) onto the filter paper disc.
Immediately place the glass chamber over the Petri dish and attach it to the metal plate using bulldog clips.

steps.title: Set Up Headspace Collection (Fruit)
steps.instruction: Assemble the chamber for fruit VOC capture.

substeps.instruction: Place filter paper (12.5 cm) on top of the metal plate.
Place orange fruit onto the filter paper.
Place the glass chamber (10 cm height × 12 cm diam.) on top of the metal plate.
Cover the outlet of the glass chamber with tin foil and create a hole using forceps.
Using cotton gloves, insert the PDMS tubing through the hole so it is suspended above the headspace.
Attach the glass chamber to the metal plate using bulldog clips.

steps.title: Set Up Rhizosphere Collection (Root VOCs)
steps.instruction: Construct a PDMS probe and prepare the growth medium.

substeps.instruction: Bend a 19 cm long glass tube (0.5 cm diam.) into a U shape (height: 8 cm, base: 3 cm) using a Bunsen burner.
Coil 130 cm of PDMS tubing around the glass tube, ensuring the inner lumen is not obstructed.
Fasten the tubing at the top of the U shape with PTFE tape.
Sterilize sand (0.25–0.71 mm grain size) in an oven at 80°C for 48 hours.
Mix sand with distilled water to achieve 15% moisture content (v/v).
Add sand to a 250 mL beaker to a depth of ca. 1 cm, place the PDMS probe on top, and fill the remainder of the beaker with sand, compacting with a metal spoon.
Transfer one 16-day-old maize plant (cv. Delprim) to the beaker.

steps.title: Set Up Rhizosphere Collection (Synthetic VOCs)
steps.instruction: Inject synthetic VOCs into the sand medium.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a synthetic VOC blend in redistilled solvent (diethyl ether/hexane) at 100 µg/µL (so 100 µL yields a 1 mg dose).
Make a 0.5 cm diam. hole in the sand medium using a hollow glass rod.
Insert a 100 µL glass micropipette to mid-depth and inject 100 µL of the blend; cover the hole with sand.
Place the PDMS tube into the beaker so it runs along opposite walls and both ends reach over the beaker rim.

steps.title: Rhizosphere Larvae Assay
steps.instruction: Introduce larvae to the root system.

substeps.instruction: Release five second instar larvae of western corn rootworm (Diabrotica v. virgifera) onto the sand surface.
Allow larvae to feed on maize roots for 5 days.

steps.title: Elute Sorbed Compounds
steps.instruction: Extract VOCs from the PDMS tubing using solvent.

substeps.instruction: Remove PDMS tubing from the headspace (using cotton gloves) or rhizosphere after the designated time (e.g., 1 hour or 5 days).
In a fume hood, clamp the PDMS tube and attach it to the end of a glass Pasteur pipette so they are suspended.
Place a 1.1 mL pointed or screw-cap GC vial underneath the tubing.
Measure 1 mL (or 2 mL for rhizosphere) of redistilled solvent (diethyl ether/hexane) into an LC-MS vial.
Pass the solvent through the clamped Pasteur pipette and PDMS tube into the GC vial.
To remove remaining solvent, attach a pipette bulb teat to the Pasteur pipette and pass a bolus of air.

steps.title: Alternative Analysis (Thermal Desorption)
steps.instruction: Prepare tubing for direct GC analysis.

substeps.instruction: Directly place the PDMS tubing into an empty Tenax tube with a glass wool plug.
Seal Tenax tubes with PDMS into glass ampoules under a stream of nitrogen.
Store at -20°C until GC/GC-MS analysis.
